$comment: HAND-AUTHORED — the register of PARKED-WITH-A-TRIPWIRE items (knowledge/_parked.py reads it, never writes it).
Born #269 2026-09-13 on Dave's word: 'store them for future sake, can they be triggered, or can we have a hook so they don't get missed at the appropriate time'.
A row is added when Dave parks something; its status moves to enacted/dropped by hand when he rules. Rows are never deleted — history is data.

Trigger kinds: pack-version-bump (due when _release/_pack_manifest.json version ≠ parked.at_version) · file-changed {path} (due when the path has a commit after parked.at_commit) · event {name} (due when that moment asks: --due <name>).

items.what: Phrase-aware RANKING in the search door — score a record higher when the query's words are ADJACENT (word bigrams via knowledge/_ngram.py), so 'six weeks' (5 verbatim) outranks 'six … weeks' (49 loose).
items.why: _search_core.py / _memento_search.py are pinned byte-identical to the memento-package by _validate_package_delta.py — a change is a pack change, therefore a RELEASE, therefore Dave's, and not before the David Rice demo. Research: _RESEARCH-ngram-lookups-2026-09-13-v1.html use 2.
items.owner: Dave (release); a lane builds once ruled

items.what: Typo tolerance in the search door — map a misspelt query word to the corpus's real word (knowledge/_ngram.py Vocabulary.nearest: 'ratifed' → 'ratified') before search runs, with the substitution shown in the receipt.
items.why: Same pin as P-269-1 — the door ships in the pack. The 'did you mean' already lives in _quote_gate.py; this is the same lookup moved into retrieval. Research use 3.
items.owner: Dave (release); a lane builds once ruled

items.what: KG edge candidates carry a measured shingle-overlap score (knowledge/_ngram.py shingles + jaccard) so proposed edges reach Dave RANKED by evidence, not bare.
items.why: At #267, 52 of 78 generated edges were wrong. Advisory ranking only — it never generates or ratifies an edge, and gen_kg_edges.py stays fenced behind lane-E RSQ 2. Research use 5. Due the next time the edge file moves.
items.owner: a lane, when the next edge batch is briefed

items.what: Dream pass opens with the near-duplicate candidate list: python3 knowledge/_near_dupes.py — 22 pairs ≥0.5 at birth, one EXACT duplicate (_GM-ARCHIVE.md:4940 = :6133).
items.why: Consolidation candidates by measurement instead of by eye. The merge is the pass's proposal and Dave's ruling. Research use 4.

items.what: Lexicon suggestions from bigram co-occurrence — propose synonym entries into a review page (never write _consult-lexicon.json).
items.why: Lowest weight of the six; only worth it after P-269-1/2 exist because it reuses their index. Research use 6.

items.what: Temporal half of ADR-0007 — decision-graph edges carry a validity window (t_valid → t_invalid, Graphiti's pattern); a superseded fact is INVALIDATED with a date, never deleted or silently demoted.
items.why: Graph-engineering research 2026-08-05 v2 item 4; notes/_STATE-MACHINE-TARGET.md §8 names it 'the named graduation path' (researched 2026-07-05, unbuilt). knowledge/_decision-graph.json has 172 edges with from/type/to/claim and no dates. Dave 2026-09-14: 'we need this recorded with tripwires'. Not before the David Rice demo.
items.owner: Dave (build decision); a lane builds once ruled

items.what: Token blast radius as a PRE-FLIGHT gate, not a report — the reach count _GRAPH-REPORT.md prints (text/default → 55 components) becomes a check a token edit must pass or declare, the way _validate_type_blast_radius.py already gates type-binding selectors.
items.why: Graph-engineering research item 5: the one place the knowledge graph starts doing control-graph work. Type half DONE (#81 cross-instrument gate); token half is still a dashboard a human reads. Due the next time the token report regenerates.

items.what: Compile views 2–6 over the typed-node graph — period/session digest · goal tree · spin-off register · tool catalog · decision trail (notes/_STATE-MACHINE-TARGET.md §7). Only view 1, the drift report, exists (_build_live_state.py).
items.why: Graph-engineering research item 6, LARGE. §7 calls these 'the point of the machine'. The §9 build-path line was stale (generator ⬜) against _build_live_state.py:136 render_lifecycle_block — corrected to PARTIAL at #269. Due at the next Memento cut or whenever the target doc moves.

items.what: Persona / job-to-be-done nodes for the super-designer — none exist and none can be relied on. Two routes Dave named: PLACEHOLDERS, or OUR OWN built on research. Shape if built: persona node with a grade field like principles (A–L, plus P = placeholder), each bound to an evidence node (finding → evidence → recommendation) so it cannot rot unnoticed; JTBD as 'Help users to…' task nodes the way GOV.UK organises patterns.
items.why: Dave 2026-09-14: 'personas and JTBD is interesting but we don't have any we can rely on, could we create placeholders, or create our own on the back of some research? I don't want to loose the idea.' Research: _PROPOSAL-kg-entity-and-edge-gaps-2026-09-14-v1.html §04 items 2 and 5; caution from C-external.json — persona sets are the ontology that rots unless bound to evidence. Due when the CX principles arrive (guidelines/ moves) or when the rules family lands in the graph.
